---
title: "Matrix Approximation"
description: "An original worked mathematical lesson corresponding to MML §4.6."
---

**Reference:** *Mathematics for Machine Learning*, Chapter 4, §4.6. The teaching example and explanation here are original.

## Why we need this concept

Compression replaces a full data matrix by a lower-rank representation that retains dominant structure. The loss can be measured explicitly instead of described as 'almost the same'.

## Derive the structure

$$
A_k=\sum_{i=1}^k\sigma_i\boldsymbol u_i\boldsymbol v_i^\top,\qquad \|A-A_k\|_F^2=\sum_{i>k}\sigma_i^2
$$

Check the shapes and conditions in this statement before applying it. The formula encodes the exact relationship to reason about, rather than replacing a derivation with a library call.

## Worked example

For A=diag(3,1), the best rank-one approximation is diag(3,0). Its squared Frobenius error is 1, while approximating with the second direction only would leave error 9.

## Interpretation and limitations

The truncated SVD minimises Frobenius reconstruction error among rank-k matrices under the usual conditions (Eckart–Young theorem). The largest singular direction is not necessarily the most interpretable business feature.

## Challenge

What fraction of squared Frobenius energy does the first singular value 3 retain when the second is 1?
